newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures close sharply higher in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures close sharply higher in Tokyo.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Wednesday's Tokyo session sharply higher, as it continued to attract bids after the recent sell-off, traders said.
The December closed up 0.69 at 124.34, just off its intraday high of 124.37.
"The December was driven higher by bargain-hunting interest, but was capped by sales from those players who were waiting to sell into strength," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
The volume of the December was 47,359 contracts.
"Investors were buying some corporate bonds, as the spread between JGBs and some of these issues has widened during the recent sell-off," said a trader at another city bank's securities unit.
Some investors were seen switching from the long-end to the intermediate sector, a trader at a long-term credit bank's securities unit said.
Swap-related buying, detected since Tuesday afternoon, was also behind today's JGB rally, traders said.
Three-year interest rate swap (IRS) rate was quoted at 1.27/1.31 percent, down from 1.37 percent on Tuesday.

"Market participants are starting to shift their focus back to economic fundamentals. They are watching carefully the upcoming industrial production data and the Bank of Japan's November 'tankan' report," said the first trader.
In the morning, JGBs were underpinned by a newspaper report, later denied, that Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) had guaranteed loans for its financially troubled non-bank unit.

The Asahi Shimbun said the bank issued a letter to agricultural financial institutions which had extended loans totalling 240 billion yen to the unit. In the letter, NCB said it would take responsibility for the unit's management.
The bank's spokesman said that while the bank had given a written statement, this did not mean it was guaranteeing the loans.

Despite the bank's denial, the report underscored the need for the Bank of Japan to maintain its easy credit policy to help financial institutions tackle their bad loan problems, traders said. -- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
